## Interpretation (hand-written)

### Fields

| Array | Assoc. | dtype / shape | Meaning | Units | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `CpMeanTrim` | cell | `<f4` (n,) | time-averaged pressure coefficient | – | paper Table 4 |
| `pMeanTrim` | cell | `<f4` (n,) | time-averaged **kinematic** pressure p/ρ, relative to p_ref = 0 at the outlet | m²/s² | paper Table 4, App. C; fit below |
| `pPrime2MeanTrim` | cell | `<f4` (n,) | variance of kinematic pressure | m⁴/s⁴ | paper Table 4 |
| `wallShearStressMeanTrim` | cell | `<f4` (n, 3) | time-averaged wall shear stress vector, kinematic (τ/ρ) | m²/s² | paper Table 4; units inferred from the OpenFOAM incompressible solver |
| `TimeValue` | field | `<f4` (1,) | 3.6 (also in the XML comment `time='3.6'`); a solver time stamp, not used | s | file |

There is **no point data**: every field lives on cells, so the surrogate predicts per
cell (cell centres + normals), and forces are Σ over cells with `boundary_cell_area_i.npy`.
"Trim" means the averaging window was trimmed to its transient-free part (paper §A.3,
MeanCalc).

### Freestream: where U∞, ρ and p∞ come from

| Quantity | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| U∞ | 38.889 m/s (140 km/h) | Ashton et al. arXiv 2408.11969, App. A; confirmed by the fit: `pMeanTrim = 756.17716 × CpMeanTrim` (R² = 1 − 2e-15) gives U∞ = sqrt(2 × 756.17716) = 38.8890 m/s |
| ρ∞ | 1 kg/m³ | paper Table 3 (value used for `force_mom*_i.csv`); with kinematic p it only matters if Pa are wanted |
| p∞ | 0 | paper App. B.2: p_ref = 0 at the outlet (x = 80 m); fit intercept 4e-9 |
| ν | 1.507e-5 m²/s (293.15 K), Re_L = 7.19e6 on the wheelbase | paper App. A |
| q∞ (kinematic) | 0.5 U∞² = 756.177 m²/s² | derived |

The VTP field data holds only `TimeValue`; none of U∞, ρ or p∞ are stored in the file.
So Cp = pMeanTrim / 756.177 exactly, and Cf = τ / 756.177 (kinematic τ, kinematic q).

### Geometry facts that matter for Day 1 (physics)

- Coordinates in metres; x is the streamwise direction (nose at x = −0.765 m, tail at
  3.938 m), z up, ground plane at z = −0.317597 m (= z of `forcesCoR`).
- Polygon normals (Newell, connectivity order) point **into the car** (signed volume < 0):
  the OpenFOAM convention, out of the fluid domain.
- The surface is watertight except at the **tyre contact patches**: 7,383 edges are used
  by a single polygon, all at z = z_min, x ∈ [−0.03, 3.01] m. Hence Σ A·n =
  (0, 0, −0.0157 m²) instead of 0. A constant pressure offset ΔCp therefore shifts Cl
  by 0.0157/aRef × ΔCp ≈ 0.0071 ΔCp (run_1) and leaves Cd and Cs unchanged. With p∞ = 0
  exactly, the fields are integrated as stored.
- Mean τ_x = −1.23 m²/s² while the flow goes +x: consistent with OpenFOAM's
  `wallShearStress`, which is the stress the wall exerts on the fluid. The sign used in the
  force integration is fixed by the Day-1 reference-force test, not assumed.
